title: Full symmetric monodromy throughout Gallagher’s weighted-lift family: An attributed Brink–Gallagher corollary
impact_reason: The uniform all-degree/all-admissible-seed monodromy observation is a useful narrow corollary, but the weighted-lift maps and degrees are Gallagher's and the free-linear-and-constant-coefficient symmetric-group theorem is Brink's.
lay_summary: An existing family of polynomial maps has the largest possible permutation symmetry among its generic inverse branches, uniformly across every allowed seed and degree.
surprise_reason: The apparent all-degree monodromy problem reduces directly to a classical theorem once the inverse equation is written in the right coordinates.
publication_reason: The author explicitly limits the contribution to combining two credited results and extending earlier finite-degree observations; this fits an attributed short note or appendix better than a new major-result article.
exact_gap: The manuscript assumes Gallagher's claimed Keller counterexamples and exact weighted-lift construction; this inventory does not independently verify that external premise. The source audit does not establish priority for the combination, and Brink supplies the group-theoretic breakthrough.
next_step: Retain as an attributed program note, group with the narrower archival monodromy note, and make the Gallagher/Brink dependency explicit in any submission or inventory description.
claim_boundary: Geometric monodromy S_d for the specified admissible Gallagher weighted lifts over C, d≥3; neither the underlying Keller counterexample discovery nor Brink's theorem is claimed as this author's invention.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript text read. Public ZIP member bytes/CRC32/size and recorded SHA256 provenance supplied by corpus audit; whole repository ZIP MD5 was not recomputed. Editorial triage only, with no fresh proof validation or novelty search.

title: The generic-degree spectrum of Keller counterexamples in dimension three: An audited, non-novel record
impact_reason: This is explicitly a non-novel attributed checkpoint: Campbell–Razar–Wright exclude degrees one/two, Trushin supplies the reproduced branch-divisor mechanism, and Gallagher supplies every higher-degree example. Its research-discovery credit is therefore zero.
lay_summary: A historical research note assembles credited results to describe which generic inverse-branch counts occur in the stated polynomial-map family.
surprise_reason: The note clarifies that generic field degree differs from polynomial degree and that taking a Galois closure does not make the original extension Galois; the headline conclusions are credited prior work.
publication_reason: Useful as exposition and provenance, but the manuscript expressly says it is not an independent discovery or new result.
exact_gap: The every-degree existence premise is imported from Gallagher's claimed counterexamples and is not independently certified here. No new research theorem is claimed, so novelty cannot be inferred from the famous problem named in the title.
next_step: Label as a historical non-novel record in the inventory and merge its explanatory material into the program notes; do not count it as another independently authored resolution.
claim_boundary: Generic function-field degree, not total polynomial degree; attributed spectrum {3,4,…} for the stated complex three-dimensional context, with universal total-degree floor still four in the note.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript text read, including priority/disclosure and credited theorem inputs. Member-level archive provenance available; no whole-ZIP digest recomputation, new proof audit or fresh novelty assertion.

title: A Cube-Component Exit for Three-Dimensional Keller Maps
impact_reason: The elementary nonsingular cube-plus-quadratic coordinate criterion is a concrete structural lemma, with bounded-degree fiberwise Keller consequences; the research-program application excludes only listed frozen families.
lay_summary: A three-variable polynomial whose highest term is one linear form cubed can be made into a coordinate whenever it has no critical point, giving a restricted invertibility test for larger polynomial maps.
surprise_reason: A short rank classification of the transverse quadratic form forces a degree-three coordinate system and inverse.
publication_reason: A concise coordinate theorem may support a specialist note, but its novelty remains unresolved and the denominator bookkeeping is best presented within a consolidated quartic/Keller program. The deposited byline withholds author information.
exact_gap: The d≤35 Keller corollary is conditional on the cited plane-degree floor108; d≤33 is the stated Moh fallback. The manuscript does not close the containing quartic rows or improve the universal degree-four floor, and the exact coordinate criterion's literature priority is unresolved.
next_step: If pursuing submission, isolate the coordinate theorem and its conservative unconditional corollary, resolve authorship/priority presentation, and keep frozen-case bookkeeping in a program appendix.
claim_boundary: Algebraically closed characteristic-zero field for f=C+ℓ³+Q₂+L₁, ℓ≠0, with no critical point; Keller exit over C requires the stated plane-degree input. Only named denominator families/pivots are covered.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript read, including rank proof, fiber reduction, conditional and fallback corollaries, finite application and limitations. No replay of verifiers or independent validation of external degree bounds.

title: Exclusion of the fixed-quadratic primitive-pencil quartic row
impact_reason: Excludes one precisely defined leading-form class of degree-four three-dimensional Keller counterexamples, using a genuine projective companion family and specialization-safe endpoint descents. It is restricted progress, not the degree-four case.
lay_summary: One possible shape of a quartic polynomial map cannot produce a counterexample: after all lower-order terms and special parameter cases are included, it must be invertible.
surprise_reason: The companion configurations form a real one-parameter projective family rather than a finite orbit list, so handling endpoints and moduli is essential to the exclusion.
publication_reason: A checkable special-case exclusion is useful, but a standalone paper organized around an internal frozen-row label has a narrower audience than a consolidated invariant theorem covering several rows.
exact_gap: Only tuple (rank JH₄,e,a,b,δ,ν)=(2,2,2,1,1,1) is excluded. Remaining quartic rows stay provisional/open; universal assertions depend on the valuation reduction, orbit exhaustiveness and exact lower-jet descents, which were not independently replayed here.
next_step: Merge with the companion fixed-linear and exact-δ exclusions into one scope-checked partial classification, translating frozen labels into invariant geometric hypotheses and retaining the exact replay packages.
claim_boundary: Exact total degree four over C, rank-two quartic leading part with fixed quadratic divisor and primitive quadratic line pencil; arbitrary lower jets retained. No full quartic exclusion or new universal degree floor.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript read, including projective-family proof, endpoint handling and computation boundaries. Member integrity provenance recorded; no fresh symbolic replay, full proof certification or worldwide priority review.

title: Exclusion of the fixed-linear primitive cubic-pencil quartic row
impact_reason: Excludes the distinct quartic leading-form tuple (2,1,3,1,1,1) by first-integral valuations, a complete root/companion atlas and lower-jet identities forcing a nonminimal boundary. The scope is one invariant row.
lay_summary: A second precisely specified leading shape cannot yield a noninvertible quartic constant-Jacobian map, even after arbitrary quadratic and cubic corrections are allowed.
surprise_reason: On the last surviving branch, a degree-six determinant identity forces the supposedly primitive cubic pencil into the wrong, nonminimal class.
publication_reason: Potentially useful special-case progress, most compelling as part of a consolidated partial quartic classification rather than another article centered on internal taxonomy.
exact_gap: The theorem does not exclude other degree-four tuples. The fifteen terminal groups and specialization-safe exact solves are load-bearing; this reading has not checked all supporting programs or established literature novelty.
next_step: Combine the invariant statement and terminal mechanism with related quartic exclusions, preserving the distinction between a plane bounded-degree theorem and the unresolved unrestricted plane problem.
claim_boundary: Degree-four Keller maps over C with rank-two leading part, fixed linear divisor and primitive cubic pencil; arbitrary lower jets. No complete degree-four result and no universal total-degree floor beyond four.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript read, including valuation descent, root atlas, final W₀≠0 elimination and external-input boundary. No new exact verifier run or independent proof/priority certification.

title: Excluding the exact-delta=4 stratum
impact_reason: A six-orbit exclusion settles one high-incidence stratum inside a fixed-quadratic line-double-cover leading family; it is narrower than an entire quartic invariant-row theorem.
lay_summary: Six special configurations in a quartic polynomial-map search are ruled out exactly, reducing one branch of the search without settling the wider problem.
surprise_reason: A Hilbert–Burch incidence bound reduces the exact-δ=4 frontier to six normal forms, but the scientific conclusion remains a tightly restricted exclusion.
publication_reason: Best retained as a certified component of a broader partial classification; the parent row and lower-incidence strata are explicitly open.
exact_gap: The theorem covers H₄=(hp²,hq²,0) with the defined exact gcd degree δ=4 only. Exact-δ=3, power-fiber and other lower-incidence families remain open; finite enumerations do not by themselves prove the universal lower-jet reductions.
next_step: Merge the six-orbit theorem and certificates into the quartic program's invariant classification, retaining separate status for the open parent row.
claim_boundary: One binary fixed-quadratic line-double-cover leading family of total-degree-four maps over C, with exact gcd stratum δ=4; no universal quartic exclusion or improvement of the degree floor.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript read, including Hilbert–Burch bound, atlas, six-descents summary and limitations. No new symbolic replay or fresh novelty assurance.

impact_reason: The actual added result is an explicit 21-dimensional witness and a nonhomogeneous scalar-parameter inversion bridge, improving a credited 22-dimensional implication; the underlying conjecture failure is imported from the prior Keller construction and is later subsumed by the author's smaller-dimensional package.
lay_summary: An explicit polynomial violates a proposed permanence property of a differential-operator kernel; the paper reduces the known construction's dimension by one.
surprise_reason: A nonhomogeneous inversion argument permits removal of a homogenizing variable while preserving infinitely many failures of the required multiplication property.
publication_reason: Preserve the archived 21-dimensional construction as historical development, but group it with the later unified 14-variable every-order obstruction package rather than treating it as an independent current conjecture disproof.
exact_gap: The noninjective stable model and determinant-pencil premise are imported from Exploration03 and the announced Keller counterexample; finite determinant specializations alone are not the universal identity. No minimum dimension or support theorem is claimed.
next_step: Link to the later unified-consequences manuscript, credit the prior Keller/Zhao/Abhyankar–Gurjar ingredients, and retain only the new nonhomogeneous bridge if it adds distinct expository value.
claim_boundary: Specific n=21 rational 72-monomial degree-four A with E(A^m)=0 for all positive m but E(Z₁A^m) nonzero infinitely often, conditional on the displayed certified-model premises. No minimality and no first general SIC-failure credit.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript read, including inversion lemma, explicit map/collision, credited predecessors and author verification disclaimer; later-family relationship supplied by corpus audit. No new checker execution or validation of the upstream Keller claim.

title: Noncommutative Comparative Statics
impact_reason: A carefully delimited modeling language organizes order-sensitive stateful repairs, directional failures and calibrated scaling, but the manuscript explicitly identifies its positive mathematics as elementary bounds or reductions to established theories and proposes a research program.
lay_summary: When a system repairs its current state after each change, applying the same changes in different orders may produce different results or make one order fail; the paper supplies a common way to describe and test that effect.
surprise_reason: It distinguishes an ordinary small outcome difference from a later hard feasibility failure near a boundary, but deliberately credits the robustness, curvature and rectification ingredients.
publication_reason: Potentially suitable as a perspective or program paper, especially paired with a concrete application; it does not yet establish a new field or an original theorem of sufficient depth for a strong standalone mathematics submission.
exact_gap: The proposed research program still needs genuinely new partial-domain stability theorems or held-out predictive evidence beyond its imported baseline sectors. The intervention presentation, metric, protocol and weights are modeling choices rather than canonical findings.
next_step: Use the framework to organize a concrete application such as permutation-cell auditing, or develop one genuinely new partial-rectification result before promoting field-level claims.
claim_boundary: Deterministic partial Lipschitz response functors on presented intervention paths, with declared metrics/protocols/amplitudes. No new invention of noncommutativity, curvature, recourse, confluence, guard robustness or Ulam stability; no empirical cross-domain validation.
review_basis: Main scientific text read through definitions, propositions, applications, limitations and conclusion; references used only for attribution as stated. Actual archive-member provenance recorded; no full external literature audit or empirical validation performed.

title: Permutation-Cell Auditing
impact_reason: Turns same-deletion-set order disagreement into a sound target-free rejection certificate, combining known metric-radius and MMD tools with exact ridge protocol analysis and a reproducible case study. The novelty is scoped applied synthesis, not the individual geometric or kernel theorems.
lay_summary: If deleting the same records in two orders produces models too far apart, at least one cannot be close to the same retrained model—even without paying to retrain. Agreement alone cannot prove successful forgetting.
surprise_reason: A service's own deletion permutations can falsify a universal retraining-equivalence claim without a retraining oracle, while a simple no-go example proves why the same idea can never positively certify forgetting.
publication_reason: A precise one-sided audit objective, controlled stochastic margin and exact solved ridge protocol give it an identifiable applied audience; operational unlearning validation beyond the illustrative case would strengthen it.
exact_gap: Only observed routes and a declared common target/law are controlled. The stochastic illustration is effect-calibrated and one-seed, not a prospective power/coverage study; no deep-model or production benchmark is supplied. Prior synthesis novelty remains unconfirmed.
next_step: Submit as a scoped audit-method paper, foregrounding common-target semantics and the impossibility of positive certification; add independent realistic unlearning-protocol evaluation if pursuing a broad machine-learning venue.
claim_boundary: Fixed nonadaptive deletion set and checkpoint with common reset target or law; finite-sample MMD assumes independent complete-route replicates within each route and predeclared selection. Affine-basis completeness needs a trusted affine promise and state injection; no privacy/deletion guarantee follows from non-rejection.
review_basis: Deposited archive-member main scientific sections read: audit semantics, radius/no-go proof, MMD theorem, contextual/affine test, ridge theorem, case study and limitations. No fresh numerical replay or external novelty audit.

surprise_reason: Both processes have the same fitness-independent limiting takeover chance1/3, and order-N^-2 terms determine endpoint failure after the leading comparison vanishes.
publication_reason: This is a distinct historical construction rather than a duplicate formula, but the headline threshold and its proposed open endpoint separator are overtaken by the later above-threshold work. Submit only as an integrated companion mechanism if the extra endpoint/class results justify it.
exact_gap: The universal upper threshold remains unproved; the archived text's open one-third affine separator at r=3/2 is now contradicted by the later family that simultaneously amplifies there. Exact module and finite-chain certificates do not alone prove the universal population asymptotics.
next_step: Link to 22089807/current above3/2 work, retain the center–triangle and endpoint computations as distinct historical results, and explicitly update the stale endpoint-separator/open-question discussion.

Class-specific portal obstructions are not universal graph theorems.

title: The Complexity of Stationary Diffusion-Driven Instability: Exact Semialgebraic Characterization, NP-Hardness, and Fixed-Species Algorithms
field: Reaction-network theory / computational complexity / mathematical biology
impact_reason: An exact arbitrary-network decision formulation, a row-family mass-action realization establishing weak NP-hardness, and polynomial bit complexity for every fixed species count together give a substantive complexity boundary distinct from the synthetic diffusion-design paper.
lay_summary: Deciding whether some positive reaction rates and diffusion choices can create stationary linear instability is computationally hard when species count grows, yet admits an exact polynomial-time algorithm when the number of species is fixed.
surprise_reason: The many reaction-flux variables can be projected into a fixed-dimensional Jacobian-factor cone, reconciling general NP-hardness with polynomial time for arbitrary reaction lists on a fixed number of species.
publication_reason: The exact characterization and matching hardness/tractability results form a coherent standalone theoretical contribution, with precise limitations and a clear distinction from nonlinear pattern formation.
exact_gap: The reduction imports Blondel–Tsitsiklis's matrix-stability mechanism and adds row splitting/right-scaling elimination plus exact mass-action realization; these interfaces and the fixed-dimensional projection algorithm need independent expert verification. Hardness for uniformly bounded or bimolecular complexes is open.
next_step: Prioritize a reaction-network/control/complexity submission, keeping the weak stationary decision problem and unbounded-molecularity reduction explicit; provide the exact input encoding and independent constructor/verifier materials.
claim_boundary: Finite indexed classical mass-action networks with positive rates/equilibrium and relative homogeneous stability; nonzero full-species diffusion modes may use the full species space despite conservation. Weak NP-hardness only, ∃R membership not ∃R-hardness, fixed-n polynomial bit complexity; no first/simple/transverse crossing, wave exclusion or nonlinear pattern theorem.
review_basis: Complete decompressed archive-member manuscript scientific text read, including characterization, Partition reduction, row realization, fixed-species algorithm, designated-mobility correction, certificate and scope sections. No fresh theorem validation, exact replay or novelty certification.
